keyConcepts.explanation: A graph that shows the cumulative total of frequencies up to each class boundary, helping to understand the accumulation of data values.
The median divides data into two equal halves, while quartiles split data into four equal parts, which can be estimated from cumulative frequency graphs.
The difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1), representing the spread of the middle 50% of data.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: In this lesson, we will learn how to use cumulative frequency graphs to find how many data values fall above or below certain thresholds. We will also explore how to interpret these graphs to compare different data sets and estimate key statistics like the median, quartiles, and interquartile range.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Using Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: If a cumulative frequency graph shows a frequency of 30 at a value of 50, what does this mean?

options: There are 30 data values greater than 50
There are 30 data values less than or equal to 50
questions.explanation: The cumulative frequency at 50 is 30 means there are 30 data values less than or equal to 50.

steps.title: Practice Question: Estimating Statistics from a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content:
A cumulative frequency graph shows total frequencies accumulating to 80 data points.

Using this graph, estimate:
1) The median
2) The first quartile (Q1)
3) The third quartile (Q3)
4) The interquartile range (IQR)

Explain how you found each value.

questions.answer: Value corresponding to cumulative frequency 40 (half of 80)
questions.explanation: Locate the cumulative frequency 40 on the y-axis and read the corresponding x-value from the graph.

questions.answer: Value corresponding to cumulative frequency 20 (one quarter of 80)
questions.explanation: Locate the cumulative frequency 20 on the y-axis and read the corresponding x-value from the graph.

questions.answer: Value corresponding to cumulative frequency 60 (three quarters of 80)
questions.explanation: Locate the cumulative frequency 60 on the y-axis and read the corresponding x-value from the graph.
Subtract the estimated Q1 value from the estimated Q3 value to find the interquartile range.
